newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open firmer.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open firmer.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open firmer Tuesday as New York and London reopened after Monday's holiday.
Gold was rangebound in lackluster overnight trading.
COMEX June gold was called $1.00 to $1.50 higher after Friday's close of $343.10 an ounce. Bullion was quoted at $343.50/$344.00 by dealers.
London gold bullion was fixed at $343.55 this morning, up $1.00 from the Friday afternoon fix.
COMEX July silver was called flat to 1.0 cent firmer.
Friday's CFTC commitments of traders report showed speculators put on more short positions in week ended May 20 compared with the previous week.
June gold was traded $345.10 to $343.10 on ACCESS.
July silver traded $4.75 to $4.725 on ACCESS.
COMEX gold stocks Friday were up 514 ounces at 874,277 ounces, while COMEX silver stocks rose 1,128,164 ounces to 196,713,292 ounces.
NYMEX July platinum was called $3.00 to $3.50 higher from Friday's close of $388.40, with NYMEX June palladium called up $3.50 to $4.00 from Friday's finish at $170.70.
U.S. existing homes sales in April, forecast at 4.09 million units on an annualised basis, are due at 1000.
